issues: The location is wrong. The locationNote says 'Place not stated on the Commons page; coordinates are a placeholder for New York' and the pin is 40.6782, -73.9442 (Brooklyn). But the Commons file page has {{Location|37.782463|-122.47187}}, re-queried through the API on 2026-09-23, and it carries the category 'Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation'. The parent file 'Aaron Swartz and Jason Scott.jpg' has the same {{Location}}. Reverse-geocoding those coordinates with OSM Nominatim gives '300, Funston Avenue, Inner Richmond, Richmond District, San Francisco', the building that houses the Internet Archive. So the photo was taken in San Francisco, not New York. The pin should use the Commons coordinates.

The caption says 'photographed by Jason Scott', which the image itself contradicts. The Commons file is a crop of 'Aaron Swartz and Jason Scott.jpg', which comes from Flickr photo 6301463398. Flickr's oEmbed API gives its title as 'Aaron Swartz and Jason Scott', from the account of Jason "Textfiles" Scott, under CC BY 2.0. In the full photo Jason Scott stands beside Swartz with his arms crossed, so he did not operate the camera. Commons credits him as author because the photo is his upload, and the creator and credit fields can keep that attribution. But the caption should not say he took the picture.

Possible context, not added to the record: 27 October 2011 was the first day of 'Books in Browsers 2011', which the Internet Archive and O'Reilly hosted at 300 Funston Ave. Jason Scott's lanyard in the parent photo reads 'Safari', an O'Reilly brand. Nothing on the Commons or Flickr records ties the photo to that event, so the caption does not claim it.
